plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the weakly dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies. Bidding higher than my value risks winning and paying more than the item is worth if others bid between my value and my bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to inform deviation, I'll bid exactly my value of $31.

This is a second-price auction with independent private values. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value, since you pay the second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you win). Bidding above your value risks paying more than the item is worth if I win against a bid between my value and my bid; bidding below reduces chances of winning profitable trades. Therefore, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid). The dominant strategy in this format is to bid exactly my true value, since bidding higher risks overpaying relative to my value if I win, and bidding lower only risks losing profitable auctions without any benefit. My value is $46, so I will bid $46 to maximize expected profit.
